text:
Sam: ran into a nasty onboarding edge case with our JS quickstart + mobile bridge. When a token refresh occurs mid-paginate + high concurrency, some page retries race and we end up with duplicated cursors and missing items. Repro below.

Yuna: ouch. is this related to the retry middleware or the pagination helper?

Sam: both. flow is: quickstart spins up 10 concurrent page requests, SDK retry logic retries immediately (exponential) but doesn't respect server Retry-After and we have no client-side limiter in the mobile bridge. When the auth refresher swaps tokens, inflight retries can get 401/429 and the paginate helper currently treats that page as failed and advances the cursor, which loses items.

Vik: interesting. Go client matches Python on concurrency defaults (4) but JS/mobile defaults to 10. That's a parity gap. Also mobile intermittently strips Retry-After headers through the proxy, so client-side limits are essential.

Sam: minimal repro curl for the mock service that returns 401 on first attempt of page n then 200 after token refresh:

```
# spawn parallel page requests
for i in {1..30}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "http://localhost:8081/items?page=$((i%6))" &\
done
wait
```

With the quickstart pattern we observed missing items ~15% of runs.

Yuna: fixes: 1) treat 401/429 as retryable in paginated helper and preserve page cursor/state until final failure; 2) add client option defaults to match Python: defaultConcurrency=4; 3) provide a small in-memory leaky-bucket + semaphore in mobile bridge. Also add honorRetryAfter flag (default true).

Vik: can we add a non-breaking "safePagination" helper in SDK first, then flip quickstart to use it? Less risky. Also emit telemetry sdk.page.retries and sdk.page.failures with a label for auth-refresh to help SRE.

Sam: yes. I'll open two PRs: sdk/js: safePagination + tests; mobile-bridge: small semaphore/token-bucket; quickstart: switch examples and short README note about concurrency.

ci-bot: build queued for sam/safe-paginate (sha: be2fc9)

Yuna: add an e2e that simulates token refresh during in-flight retries and asserts no items lost. Also add a sample showing p-limit pattern for users who need to parallelize more aggressively.

Vik: from infra we can try to make Retry-After consistent but can't rely on it everywhere. We'll add a dashboard panel for sustained 429s and token-refresh spikes to help identify client misconfig.

Sam: filed internal issue https://redwood-internal/issues/5402 and added a short checklist for PR reviewers to verify telemetry labels.

Yuna: thanks. small change but high impact for PLG onboarding and mobile users.

Vik: noted. once PRs are up ping security if token-rotation tests touch auth libraries.

Sam: will do. closing for now — will paste PR links when available.
